clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle Control
clusters.description: Architectural choices for modeling rental states, durations, transitions, and scheduled lifecycle actions, distinct from how updates are distributed.

relations.rationale: Rental transitions, duration thresholds, and expiry actions produce state changes that downstream components may need to receive.

values.label: State-based rental lifecycle model
values.description: Represents rental lifecycle transitions explicitly as state-dependent behavior.

values.label: Scheduler-driven duration and expiry control
values.description: Tracks elapsed rental time and schedules notifications before expiry or other lifecycle deadlines.

clusters.name: Event Propagation Strategy
clusters.description: Choices for propagating bike, rental, history, and interface updates, distinct from the business lifecycle logic generating those updates.

relations.rationale: Lifecycle state changes require a propagation mechanism so web, mobile, history, and monitoring consumers receive relevant updates.

values.label: Observer-based bike status propagation
values.description: Uses observers or subscribers to broadcast bike status changes to interested components.

values.label: Asynchronous rental state notification
values.description: Publishes rental state changes asynchronously to user-interface components and other subscribers.

values.label: Usage-history event notification
values.description: Notifies subscribers when usage or trip history changes.

clusters.name: Fleet Location Discovery
clusters.description: Choices for representing bike positions and answering radius-based availability queries, distinct from rental state and event delivery.

values.label: Location-based proximity discovery
values.description: Maintains bike locations and supports proximity queries for discovering available rentals within the rider’s nearby radius.

clusters.name: Authentication Security Controls
clusters.description: Choices for authenticating riders and controlling credential, token, and session protection, distinct from rental and fleet behavior.

values.label: Email-password authentication
values.description: Uses email and password as the primary rider authentication credentials.

values.label: Credential transmission and storage protection
values.description: Protects credentials during transmission and storage.

values.label: Session termination and token expiration
values.description: Provides immediate user-controlled logout and limits verification-token validity to a short period.

clusters.name: Authentication and Session Security
clusters.description: Choices for rider authentication, biometric access, credential protection, session termination, and token validity.

relations.rationale: Registration credentials and identity verification establish the account context required for authentication and session controls.

values.label: Email-password authentication

values.label: Inactivity-based session timeout

clusters.name: Usage Reporting Strategy
clusters.description: Choices for assembling, transforming, and delivering user-facing usage-history reports from operational trip data.

relations.rationale: Reports depend on accumulated usage or trip history being available as an input dataset.

values.label: Builder-based downloadable usage reporting
values.description: Builds downloadable user usage-history reports from usage data using a Builder-based assembly process.

clusters.name: Operational Observability Strategy
clusters.description: Choices for aggregating operational data and exposing live fleet conditions for monitoring, diagnostics, and management.

relations.rationale: Live operational visibility relies on status and usage events being propagated to dashboards or monitoring subscribers.

values.label: Real-time fleet monitoring and usage aggregation
values.description: Aggregates usage data and pushes real-time bike status to dashboards and monitoring components for fleet oversight.

clusters.name: Registration Data Governance
clusters.description: Choices for collecting, validating, securing, and minimizing personal information during rider account registration.

relations.rationale: Registration data collection establishes the personal and credential information later protected by authentication and session controls.

values.label: Validated and secure registration-data capture
values.description: Collects identity and contact information, optionally postal code, requires credentials, validates input, and securely submits registration data.

clusters.name: Domain Workflow Coordination
clusters.description: Choices for coordinating domain workflows such as bike registration and removal through synchronous or asynchronous events.

relations.rationale: Event-driven bike workflows emit domain changes that can subsequently be delivered to dependent services and consumers.

values.label: Event-driven bike registration and removal
values.description: Coordinates bike registration through events and triggers bike removal with asynchronous event-based processing.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. Rental duration tracking and pre-expiry notification scheduling fit dimension 1 (Rental Lifecycle Control), specifically scheduler-driven duration/expiry control. Manual session termination control and short verification-token expiration fit dimension 4 (Authentication Security Controls), specifically session termination and token expiration. Observer-based bike status notification, usage-history event notification, and asynchronous/UI notifications are covered by dimension 2 (Event Propagation Strategy). Location-based bike tracking, proximity query handling, and nearby rental discovery are covered by dimension 3 (Fleet Location Discovery). Email-password authentication, secure transmission for credentials, and secure storage of credentials are all within dimension 4. The remaining labels are either restatements of these same concerns or implementation glosses that do not introduce a new architectural axis relevant to the CityBike use case. Therefore no genuinely uncovered concept remains in this minibatch.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions in the taxonomy. Usage-history report generation, Builder-based assembly, and report-from-usage-data all fit Dimension 5 (Usage Reporting Strategy). Real-time bike status monitoring, usage data aggregation, operational visibility, dashboard updates, and monitoring subscriptions fit Dimension 6 (Operational Observability Strategy) and, where applicable, Dimension 2 (Event Propagation Strategy). Thumbprint authentication and post-authentication biometric deletion fit Dimension 4 (Authentication and Session Security). Registration-time identity/contact capture, credentials, optional postal code, secure submission, and input validation fit Dimension 7 (Registration Data Governance). Inactivity timeout and automatic logout fit Dimension 4 as session controls. Observer-based bike status push notifications fit Dimension 2. The state machine, QR unlock transition, rental lifecycle state management, and ride tracking state handling are covered by Dimension 1 (Rental Lifecycle Control) for lifecycle/state modeling, while the event-driven bike registration workflow and asynchronous bike removal fit Dimension 8 (Domain Workflow Coordination). No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural concern beyond these existing axes for the CityBike design space.
